notes_for_editor: Thin primary coverage: Light-House Board reports before 1891 are not in the corpus, so the 1873 appropriation, 1874-75 construction and wreck details rest on the NRHP nomination and LighthouseFriends (copyrighted; paraphrased). Disagreements stated in the text: Aculeo date (Oct 17 vs Nov 1872), 1912 lens structure (wood frame vs iron skeletal), Fresnel removal (1962 vs 1970), tower material (steel vs cast iron), and Mayo Beach dates. Rydal Hall date is derived from LighthouseFriends's 'four years to the day'. Commissioner volume page 79 (labelled 1922 in the corpus; fiscal year of the estimate not confirmed). Left out on purpose: the 1909 criminal conviction of head keeper Henry Hall (LighthouseFriends, newspaper-derived, concerns a minor) and the personal marriage story of Luff. LighthouseFriends also spells Patterson 'Edward'. The 1919 and 1893 page numbers: 1893 report printed page unconfirmed ('168?'); 1919 report p. 89 confirmed by scan. HI USA blog calls the tower cast iron and says the tower was built near Boston; not used. Wikipedia says the lens is at College of Notre Dame library; not used (conflicts with LighthouseFriends). The 1896-97 volume does not say which year the sounding board was added (LighthouseFriends says 1897). Corrections: none; USLHS height 55 ft focal vs record 21.3 m (70 ft) - NRHP says bluff is 70 ft above ocean, USLHS 'height of light above water 55'. No keeper roster matches were made by position from OCR tables.
